source: CoreGuard Quilla Cyber Codex (original educational summaries; cites public frameworks)

entries.title: OWASP MASVS v2 — Mobile security baseline
entries.summary: Industry baseline for mobile app security controls across 8 categories.
entries.body: OWASP MASVS v2 organizes mobile app security into eight control categories: STORAGE, CRYPTO, AUTH, NETWORK, PLATFORM, CODE, RESILIENCE, and PRIVACY. Use it as the requirements layer; map tests with MASTG. CoreGuard Compliance scores against MASVS-inspired checks for this device's posture.
entries.defense: Run CoreGuard Compliance, remediate FAIL/WARN checks, then re-score. Prefer threat-model-driven profiles (L1/L2/R/P) over checkbox theater.

entries.title: MASVS-STORAGE — Data at rest
entries.summary: Protect sensitive data stored on the device.
entries.body: Sensitive tokens, PII, and secrets must not sit in plaintext app storage, backups, or world-readable paths. Prefer Android Keystore-backed keys, encrypted files/prefs, and minimal retention. Check logs and screenshots for accidental leakage.
entries.defense: Audit app data dirs, disable unnecessary backups for sensitive apps, and clear leftover exports after Compliance JSON use.

entries.title: MASVS-CRYPTO — Cryptography
entries.summary: Use modern cryptography correctly; avoid homemade crypto.
entries.body: Use platform crypto APIs and vetted libraries. Prefer AEAD modes, reject weak ciphers/hashes, manage keys in Keystore/StrongBox when available, and never hardcode secrets. Randomness must come from secure generators.
entries.defense: Flag custom crypto, static keys in APKs, and outdated TLS stacks during supply-chain and code reviews.

entries.title: MASVS-AUTH — Authentication & authorization
entries.summary: Prove identity and enforce least privilege on sensitive operations.
entries.body: Secure login, token lifecycle, biometric step-up for high-risk actions, and server-side authorization. Local biometrics unlock keys; they are not a remote auth substitute. Invalidate sessions on logout and device change.
entries.defense: Review session storage, refresh-token handling, and whether critical actions require re-auth.

entries.title: MASVS-NETWORK — Data in transit
entries.summary: Encrypt and authenticate traffic to backends.
entries.body: Disable cleartext by default (network security config), use modern TLS, validate certificates properly, and consider pinning for high-risk apps. Watch for debug proxies left enabled in release builds.
entries.defense: CoreGuard Shield DNS filtering complements, but does not replace, TLS. Scan for cleartext and review Network Security Config.

entries.title: MASVS-PLATFORM — Platform & IPC
entries.summary: Secure interaction with Android components and other apps.
entries.body: Exported activities/services/receivers/providers are attack surface. Validate intents and deep links, constrain WebViews, and treat inter-app data as untrusted. Permission requests must match least privilege.
entries.defense: Inventory exported components and deep-link handlers; remove unused exports.

entries.title: MASVS-CODE — Secure coding & updates
entries.summary: Keep code, platform target, and dependencies healthy.
entries.body: Validate inputs, keep min/target SDK current, patch libraries, and ship update paths users can actually use. Third-party SDKs expand attack surface — track them with SBOM-style inventories.
entries.defense: Use CoreGuard supply-chain / SDK awareness where available; prefer Play updates and verified sources.

entries.title: MASVS-RESILIENCE — Anti-tamper & RE resistance
entries.summary: Raise cost of reverse engineering and runtime abuse.
entries.body: Resilience includes integrity checks, anti-debug/anti-hook heuristics, and obfuscation — always layered with server trust, never as the only control. Rooted/emulated environments deserve elevated risk scores.
entries.defense: CoreGuard already probes debugger/emulator/root/Frida-style signals as posture inputs, not magic spyware detectors.

entries.title: MASVS-PRIVACY — User privacy controls
entries.summary: Minimize collection and make processing transparent.
entries.body: Collect least data, purpose-limit processing, disclose practices, and honor platform privacy features. Avoid fingerprinting beyond necessity. On-device processing is a privacy win when it replaces cloud telemetry.
entries.defense: CoreGuard scans run on-device; prefer that model for sensitive workflows.

entries.title: OWASP MASTG — How mobile apps get tested
entries.summary: Testing guide that maps MASVS controls to practical test cases.
entries.body: MASTG covers static analysis (APK/IPA review), dynamic analysis (runtime instrumentation), network testing, and platform abuse cases. Profiles (L1/L2/R/P) help scope effort to risk. Ethical testing requires authorization.
entries.defense: For personal devices, use CoreGuard's on-device checks first; commissioned pentests need written scope and rules of engagement.
